p.i: Thurus ad Enshemum leviore nec Ombacus unda
Phacidos hinc undam Colmaria mancipat Ello
Auctior ad Rhenum ductile flectit iter.
Excipit ad lævam sinuosi flumina Prusis,
Prusis ab occiduo defluit orbe satus.
Alluit argento qua nomina mutuat, urbem,
Quod removet, Rheni labra subire dedit.
Inde decem passus descendunt flumina Rheni
Mille, videt Sornam Rhenus adesse sibi.
Qui latias adiit fluvio simul atque Tabernas
Yennichis occurrit, qui nomine nominat urbem
Vrbs procul à Rheno, Zephyri declinat ad oras
Cum subigit læva Benhemia margine ripa
Sex simulac gressu superavit millia passum
Dum sua confini Lutterus nomina Castro
Mancipat, hunc Rheni gurgite læva tegit.
Rhenus adhuc restat signa videre loci.
Solis ad occasum nomina montis habent.
Parva tamen gestit dote superba loci.
Hinc latus ad dextrum subit Vdenhemia, Rhenus
Quattuor ut passum millia carpsit iter.
Altius ad lævam Nemeti stant fluminis ora

page.notes: Marginal black-letter place names read as "Markgraven Baden", "Rheinzabern", "Berghzabern" (the printed forms are in Fraktur; spelling approximate). Verse lines are printed in italic with a few doubtful letters (e.g. "Yennichis", "Srectanum", "Prusis"), copied as seen. The word "Cratia" at lower right is a catchword. Some marginal notes are attached to the line ends where they stand.
